data.text:
**Timeline reconstructed:**

- **02:01:44** — modem logged `No Ranging Response received - T3 time-out` → lost upstream sync (`NOT_SYNCHRONIZED`); internet went down ~02:01.
- **02:06 / 02:29** — watchdog saw `modem_not_operational`, then `modem_settling`; correctly took no action.
- **02:28:21** — modem completed reboot/registration; back to `OPERATIONAL` (SNR ~37.6–37.9 dB, healthy).
- **02:30 and 02:40** — watchdog decided `reload` / `retry`, but it runs in **observe mode**, so only `would_reload` was recorded — the WAN interface was never actually reconfigured.

Meanwhile on gw.lan: WAN has address 198.51.100.27 from an old DHCP lease (server-id 203.0.113.67), the default route points at 198.51.100.1 with a stale ARP entry, yet pings to the ISP gateway show **100% loss**. The ISP link itself is up again (modem registered), but the firewall's WAN session is stale and nothing has renewed it.

data.reason: Modem is back OPERATIONAL since 02:28 (registered, good SNR per /var/db/wan-watchdog/modem-metrics.jsonl and modem-events.jsonl), but the firewall's WAN still holds a stale DHCP session from before the outage; the watchdog logged reload decisions at 02:30/02:40 but only "would_reload" because it is in observe mode. Pinging the ISP gateway 198.51.100.1 fails 100%. Reconfiguring the WAN interface / renewing the DHCP lease should re-establish the ISP session now that the cable plant is healthy.

data.error: action must be one of: change_config, contact_provider, investigate_further, none, reboot_host, replace_hardware, restart_service
host must be one of: gw.lan, mon.lan, external

data.component: WAN interface / DHCP session on gw.lan (stale after ISP-side modem outage)
data.cause: The internet dropped when the cable modem lost upstream sync (T3 timeout at 02:01:44); the modem re-registered and became OPERATIONAL at 02:28, but the firewall's WAN interface kept its stale pre-outage DHCP session — the watchdog wanted to reload it at 02:30/02:40 but runs in observe mode, so no renewal ever happened.
evidence: /var/db/wan-watchdog/modem-events.jsonl: 'No Ranging Response received - T3 time-out' at 02:01:44 and 'Cable Modem Reboot ... registration complete' at 02:28:21, matching the outage window starting ~02:01
/var/db/wan-watchdog/modem-metrics.jsonl: cm_status NOT_SYNCHRONIZED at 02:06, then OPERATIONAL with healthy SNR (~37.6-37.9 dB) from 02:29 onward — the ISP link itself recovered

/var/db/wan-watchdog/events.jsonl: decisions 'modem_not_operational' (02:06) and 'modem_settling' (02:29), then action 'reload' at 02:30 and 'retry' at 02:40 recorded only as 'would_reload' with mode=observe — no actual reload was performed
ifconfig vtnet0: WAN still up with address 198.51.100.27; /var/db/dhclient.leases.vtnet0 shows a long-lived lease (renew not due until 2026/3/5), so DHCP would not have renewed on its own
ping -c 3 198.51.100.1: 100% packet loss to the ISP gateway despite an ARP entry for it, while local hosts (e.g. 10.20.0.9 via vtnet1) are in the table — fault is at the WAN handoff, not the LAN
data.recommendation: Renew the WAN interface configuration (wan_reload, already requested and preconditions met) to replace the stale DHCP session now that the modem is re-registered and OPERATIONAL. Longer term, let the watchdog actually perform the reload once the modem reports OPERATIONAL and has settled, instead of only logging 'would_reload' in observe mode.
